idiom_name: amqp091-go Channel.Consume -> <-chan amqp.Delivery ranged in a goroutine
implementation_notes: Go's idiom dissolves the endpoint object into a channel: amqp091-go's ch.Consume(...) returns a native <-chan Delivery, and the endpoint becomes a goroutine ranging over that channel with d.Ack(false)/d.Nack(false, requeue) carrying the semantics. This replaces the classic onMessage endpoint class with a goroutine plus a channel; keep an explicit endpoint type when you need per-consumer state, reconnect supervision or lifecycle management, because the range loop simply ends when the delivery channel closes (kafka-go's reader loop and nats.go subscriptions have the same shape).
pitfalls: The delivery channel closes when the consumer is cancelled or the connection drops; without a supervisor that re-registers the consumer, the endpoint silently stops receiving.
Ack/Nack must be called exactly once per delivery: double acks, or acks issued on another channel, are protocol errors that close the channel.
amqp091-go channels are not safe for concurrent use; use one channel per consumer goroutine or serialise all channel operations.
auto-ack (third Consume argument true) acknowledges before the handler runs, trading at-least-once for message loss.
